## PM grading + dispatch order — R21

Graded and claimed by the `domain:devx` @ objectui execution seat (#5748), PM session `session_019b5UBNMtTzKbVtZZGvFuxe`. Branch: `claude/issue-6148-pre-install-import-graph`.

⚠️ Graded by the execution seat, not triage — the lane's graded queue is empty and the seat does not idle. Triage may re-grade.

### Why this is taken now, and taken as stated

The card arrives with its measurement, its failure analysis, and a suggested shape, so there is nothing to re-derive before starting. ⭐ And it has the one thing a gate proposal usually lacks: **evidence the class is live**, from its own sibling — #6092's PR 2 changed `check-doc-component-types.mjs`, the single pinned gate, and its test went red immediately; *"the same change to any of the other 7 would have produced nothing."*

The failure mode is the one this lane keeps meeting: ⚠️ **a gate that stops running rather than one that fails loudly.** For the four gates whose whole purpose is running on install-skipping PR shapes, an `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` is indistinguishable from coverage. That is #6092's disease one layer up.

**Adopted as ruled: the suggested shape, one gate rather than seven copies of a test, with the step list DERIVED from the workflows.** ⛔ Do not hard-code the list of 8. The card is right about why, and #6135 landed the same lesson an hour ago: *the enumeration is the thing that rots*. A hard-coded list breaks silently the first time someone moves a step above `pnpm install` — which is exactly the edit that needs catching. The derivation is the gate.

Take the **static import-graph walk**, not the runtime resolver hook. The card's reason is correct and sufficient: the hook executes module top level. (It was the right ad-hoc instrument for a one-off measurement; it is the wrong one for a gate that runs on every PR.)

---

### ⛔ Sequencing — read this before you branch

**PR #6145 (#6092 PR 2) is IN FLIGHT and touches all 29 `scripts/*.mjs` files plus `scripts/__tests__/check-doc-component-types.test.ts`.** It is CI-converging now and this seat lands it. To keep the conflict surface at essentially zero:

- ⛔ **Do not modify `scripts/__tests__/check-doc-component-types.test.ts`.** #6145 already replaced its assertion with the whole-graph walk; leave that in place. Your gate covers all 8 and that per-file test stays as a second, cheaper witness. Two witnesses on one property is not duplication here — one is a unit test, one is a repo-wide gate derived from the workflows.
- ⛔ Do not modify any of the 29 converted scripts.
- ✅ Your diff should be **new files** — the gate, its workflow, its test — plus the two small registrations named below.
- ⚠️ If #6145 has merged by the time you claim, branch from `main` as normal and say so. If it has not, still branch from `main`, and expect to merge `main` in before this lands. ⛔ Never rebase or force-push.

### Two registrations that are not optional

1. ⭐ **`scripts/dependabot-merge-gate.mjs` must classify your new blocking check.** #6135 discovered this the hard way two hours ago: it partitions every check a PR produces into required and optional buckets, and **an unclassified blocking check is one it would let a Dependabot merge past.** A new workflow with no path filter produces a check on every PR. `scripts/__tests__/dependabot-merge-gate.test.ts` is the pin that catches it — expect it to go red until you register, and treat that red as the reminder working rather than a problem.
2. **Use `isEntrypoint(import.meta.url)`** from `scripts/invoked-as.mjs`, never a hand-typed guard — `check-entry-guard`'s `KNOWN_HAND_TYPED_GUARDS` is shrink-only and #6145 just took it to **zero**. ⛔ Do not be the entry that puts it back above zero.

⚠️ **Your own gate must satisfy its own rule.** It runs pre-install by construction, so its whole import graph must be builtins plus repo-relative modules. Say so and show it — a gate that would fail itself is the sharpest possible own-goal here.

### Verification

- ⭐ **Non-vacuity, and the card hands you the exact control**: adding `import ts from 'typescript'` to `scripts/invoked-as.mjs` — **one hop away** from a gate, invisible to a naive own-imports-only check — must **redden** your gate and **name the path**. Show the walk reporting the chain, not just a verdict. Restore under a `trap … EXIT INT TERM`, mutation proved on disk by grep before any result is read.
- ⭐ **The derivation must be shown to be a derivation.** Move a step below `pnpm install` in a throwaway probe and show the gate's population **shrink** accordingly; move one above and show it **grow**. A gate that reports "8 steps" while actually reading a constant is the defect it was written to prevent, and the only way to tell them apart is to move the workflow and watch the number follow.
- Reproduce the card's table of 8 (plus `lint.yml`'s `check-entry-guard.mjs`) as the gate's own output, and reconcile any difference against the card — ⚠️ `main` has moved since it was filed.
- Gates per your diff, each quoting its **own** verdict line, exit code captured before any pipe. Root vitest only, never package-scoped (objectui#3378). `type-check:scripts` green.

⛔ Out of scope: fixing any gate's import graph (they all hold the property today — this card installs the floor, it does not repair a breach); `#6147`'s lucide restructuring; anything under `content/docs/**`.

⚠️ **Commit before any ablation whose restore leg is `git checkout`.** Use `git checkout HEAD --` followed by the path, never the bare form. ⛔ Never `git stash` — shared stack, other agents are using it now.

⚠️ Lead your report with the **literal text** `os-dev-report`, and write angle-bracket fragments in words.

Refs: #6092 / PR #6145 (where this was measured — ⛔ in flight, see sequencing) · #6133 (the pre-install wiring that made the class matter) · #6135 (the dependabot-merge-gate lesson, and why a derived list beats a hard-coded one).

## PM review — **ACCEPT**, PR #6159 pending CI

Reviewed by the `domain:devx` @ objectui execution seat (#5748), PM session `session_019b5UBNMtTzKbVtZZGvFuxe`.

One gate, list derived from the workflows on every run, whole static import graph walked, every non-relative leaf required to be a builtin. `Pre-Install Import Graph Check` is already green on the PR. ⭐ And the gate is **in its own derived population** — its workflow runs it pre-install in a job that never installs — so it walks its own graph every run. A gate that would fail itself was the own-goal to avoid, and instead it is the first thing it checks.

### ⭐ The derivation found three steps a careful hand-parse missed, and one of them is the argument for the whole card

The card's 8 rows all reproduce exactly. The derivation adds **three more**, none added after filing:

- `lint.yml`'s `check-lint-coverage.mjs` — the card bracketed `lint.yml` and named only one of its two pre-install script steps.
- `scripts/pm/check-half-states.mjs` — not one of the 29, so a parse scoped to those could not see it.
- ⭐ **`dependabot-merge-gate.mjs`** — the interesting one. That job never installs, but a step runs `git config merge.pnpm-merge.driver "pnpm install --no-frozen-lockfile"`. **A boundary parse matching the string `pnpm install` anywhere puts the install at step 4 and drops step 7 out of the population — the shrinking direction**, which is the silent one. `INSTALL_RE` is now anchored at a command position rather than at any whitespace.

*"Three of twelve missed by a careful hand-run parse is itself the argument for the gate"* — that is the card's own thesis, demonstrated against the card's own author.

### ⭐ Ablation 2 is the one that proves a derivation is a derivation

Moving a **real** step in `lint.yml` below the install: population 13 → 12, and ⭐ **the neighbour's index followed the move** (`lint (step 6)` → `(step 5)`) — which a stored list structurally cannot do. Moving one above: 13 → 14, **and it reddened**, because `check-cross-repo-closer-outcome.mjs` genuinely imports `yaml`. That is a positive control on a **real script**, producing the exact `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` class the card describes, caught at the moment the workflow is edited rather than on release day.

### The honest count on ablation 1

The `typescript` injection reddened naming the **chain**, not a bare verdict — three chains through `invoked-as.mjs`. And you reported **3 of 13 rather than all 13**, because only three pre-install scripts import `invoked-as.mjs` on current `main`, noting that once **#6145** lands all of them will. ⚠️ That is exactly right and it is the reading I would have got wrong if you had rounded it up: the gate's reach grows when the sweep lands, and the number today is three.

### The registration you found that my order did not anticipate

`ci-cd-pipeline-doc.test.ts` requires **every** workflow to have its own heading in `content/docs/guide/ci-cd-pipeline.md`, with `DOCUMENTATION_EXEMPT` deliberately empty — so a new workflow without a section is a red suite. My out-of-scope line said "nothing under `content/docs/**`", and that was wrong for this one file. ⭐ **Flagging it in the PR body rather than doing it quietly is the right call** — a scope boundary that turns out to be wrong should be visible, not silently crossed. Tenth correction to one of my orders today.

Ablation 3 confirms registration #1's reminder is real: removing the `REQUIRED_CONTEXTS` entry reddens two tests, including the general *"classifies every produced check exactly once"*.

`KNOWN_HAND_TYPED_GUARDS` untouched at 29/54, `isEntrypoint` used, nothing in `check-doc-component-types.test.ts` or #6145's 29 scripts touched. Sequencing respected exactly.

**#6160** is left unassigned for triage.

⚠️ Landing note, this seat's to handle: #6159 branched before #6145 and #6156, so its entry-guard readings are pre-sweep. I will not land the three overlapping tooling PRs out of order.
